grades.why: It presents `--legacy-env false` / `legacy_env = false` as a working way to deploy to service environments, when the key says the flag and field are gone and every environment now deploys as `<name>-<environment>`.
It omits DO_NOT_TRACK=1 and presents the stale WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS/telemetry disable approach as the way to turn off telemetry, claiming the env var wins.
It claims there is no `us` jurisdiction and only eu/fedramp exist, which is the stale answer, instead of giving `--jurisdiction us`.
It states the stale behavior that --latest sets the compatibility date to today's date, rather than the newest date the bundled workerd supports.
It says to remove the positive flags and set both no_nodejs_compat and no_nodejs_compat_v2 for dates 2026-08-04 or later, which matches the key, and it doesn't present the stale behavior.
It says there is no setting to keep objects on old code after a deploy, which is the stale claim, and it misses the deferred code update strategy that is now the default.
It states the single 64 MiB uncompressed limit, that the uncompressed upload size is what counts (gzip informational), and describes the 3/10 MB limits as removed, not current.

It states wrangler dev captures traces and console logs into the Local Explorer Observability tab by default and that X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY=false opts out, mentioning the opt-in behavior only as pre-4.118.0 history.
It says Workers cannot accept inbound raw TCP, which is the stale answer, and it never mentions the experimental local-only `connect` config entry or handler.
It presents the stale `wrangler r2 sql` path and `WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN` as current instead of `wrangler basin sql` with `WRANGLER_BASIN_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN`.
It says Workflows have no per-workflow concurrency setting and only account limits apply, which is the stale behavior, and it never mentions `workflows[].concurrency.limit`.
It claims the endpoints are under `/cdn-cgi/mf/` rather than `/cdn-cgi/local/`, and it also presents the stale `/cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled` path as a current option.
It says queues are not created automatically, which contradicts the key's statement that provisioning now covers Queue bindings.
It says the command is no longer alpha and reports bundle size plus a local CPU timing summary; mentioning the .cpuprofile file doesn't claim that's all it does.
It asserts as current that bulk can only create or update secrets and says to delete with `wrangler versions secret delete`, which is the stale behavior; it doesn't mention setting the value to null.
It says there is no official terminal client and misses `npx agents tui <url>`, which matches the stale answer.

It says Agents must be addressed by name and that RPC on newUniqueId() stubs fails, which matches the key, though it hedges and gives a slightly different reason (missing name rather than lifecycle initialization).
It doubts `agents/channels` but never gives the `agents/experimental/channels` path, and instead points the user to other docs and package exports.
It says getCurrentAgent() inside queued callbacks returns the agent but connection and request are undefined, which matches the key and avoids the stale claim.
It states useAgent takes a transport option with "cf-websocket" (default, hibernating) or experimental "capnweb" using a Cap'n Web session with native RPC stubs, matching the key.
It states useAgentChat throttles to 50ms by default, with `throttle: false` to render every chunk or a number to change the interval, and mentions `experimental_throttle` only as a deprecated alias.
It states the second argument is the parsed Schedule object (with id, callback, type, timing fields) and does not present the raw storage row with a JSON-string payload as current.

It says scheduling is only available via `this.schedule()` on an Agent subclass, which is the stale behavior, and it never mentions the `Scheduler` capability from `agents/schedules` that any Durable Object can use.
It says Agent now extends Cloudflare's DurableObject directly rather than PartyServer's Server, which matches the key; it omits the agents/lifecycle vendoring detail but states nothing false.
It directs the user to wrapAISDK() from agents/observability/ai for both AI SDK v6 and v7, calls createAISDKTelemetry an old or wrong name, and never presents the stale API as current.
It says there is no storage option and that the manager gets storage from the Lifecycle/Durable Object it is installed on, matching the key.
It says createMcpHandler takes a factory returning a v2 McpServer and serves statelessly, with createLegacyMcpHandler kept for SDK v1, and it does not present the v1 pattern as current.
It says subAgent() is deprecated and avoids the stale advice, but admits it doesn't know the replacement and omits this.dynamicAgents and facets, so it doesn't meet the key.
It says the client opens with an `initialize` handshake, which is the stale behavior, and never mentions probing with `server/discover` first.
It presents the stale behavior (only a warning) as current and does not say the un-awaited assertion fails the test.
It says Vitest walks up parent directories to find the config, which is the stale behavior; per the key, Vitest 5 only looks in the project root.
It claims @vitest/runner is still an internal dependency of vitest and suggests using it directly (pinned) for standalone tools, missing that it is deprecated and no longer used by Vitest 5.
It states the stale default .vitest-reports/ instead of .vitest/blob/.
It says toHaveTextContent passes on substring matches, which is the stale behavior, instead of strict matching with toMatchTextContent for partial matches.
It correctly says agents supports ai@^6 || ^7, but it wrongly implies @cloudflare/think works on ai@6 when the key says Think now requires ai@^7 only.
It gives the stale setup, calling it Vitest's own provider, and never says it moved to the vitest-community organization or that version 5.0.0 works with Vitest 5.
It says getByText does substring matching by default, which is the stale behavior; the key says locators.exact defaults to true.
It states the stale behavior that inline projects don't inherit the root config unless `extends: true` is set, whereas the key says they inherit by default.
It says describe and test names are joined by spaces, which is the stale behavior, instead of the current `>` separator.
It claims Vitest has no built-in argument matcher and recommends mockImplementation, which is the stale answer, rather than Vitest 5's vi.when().
The answer says expect.poll fails with a timeout error when the function doesn't resolve, including for Vitest, and its hang-only-with-timeout-0 caveat isn't the stale claim.
It states the stale claim that --project has no short alias, while the key says -p is the shorthand.
It never says the call now throws an error, and it presents hoisting with unconditional execution as possible current behavior, which is the stale answer.
It says the CLI has no repeat flag and that repeats can only be set per test, which is the stale behavior; it never mentions `--repeats`.
It says vitest list loads and executes test files to collect tests, which is the stale behavior; the key says it parses them statically by default.
